https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Director Sam Mendes’s next film after his 1999 Best Picture winner American Beauty is a somber and gorgeously crafted gangster drama, based on a graphic novel series by Max Allan Collins and Richard Piers Rayner. Tom Hanks plays Michael Sullivan, a loving father and stoic enforcer for an Irish-American crime family (led by supporting actor nominee Paul Newman), who must flee with his young son. Conrad L. Hall won a posthumous Oscar for his dark, moody cinematography, and the film was also nominated for its art direction (Dennis Gassner, Nancy Haigh), Thomas Newman’s moving score, and the atmospheric contributions of supervising sound editor Scott A. Hecker and sound mixers Scott Millan, Bob Beemer and John Patrick Pritchett.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Sam Mendes PRODUCED BY: Richard D. Zanuck, Dean Zanuck, Sam Mendes

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Made for less than $20,000 just after the liberation of Italy by US forces, Rossellini’s first installment in his Neo-Realist Trilogy, which also includes Paisan (1946, screening on November 15) and Germany, Year Zero (1948, screening the same day), is also considered the first product of neo-realism. The devastation of Nazi-occupied Rome serves as an all-too-real backdrop for a story that could have been ripped from the headlines: a resistance leader (Aldo Fabrizi) is pursued through town as he seeks shelter and a safe escape. With “the terror of German occupation [...] still vivid in the minds of everyone,” (Patrizio Rossi, 1988) including Rossellini’s lead actress, the great Anna Magnani, Rome, Open City serves as a prototype for a series of films that characterize the best of Italian cinema.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Roberto Rossellini

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Baz Luhrmann’s take on Shakespeare’s tragedy is perhaps one of the best-loved adaptations and is the second installment in his Red Curtain Trilogy, which closed with Moulin Rouge! (2001). Featuring Luhrmann’s distinctive, stylized palate coupled with frenetic, MTV-style editing and an all-star soundtrack, Romeo + Juliet became a classic for its casting, with Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes playing the star-crossed lovers.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Baz Luhrmann

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: “Neo-realism is above all a moral standpoint from which to look at the world,” Roberto Rossellini proclaimed in 1954, and this conviction led him not just to make lasting contributions to the neo-realist mode, but also equipped him to articulate his artistic ideas into spoken language. In this loving documentary portrait of the father of the cinematic movement, scholar Adriano Aprà uses archival footage and interviews with Rossellini to underscore the filmmaker’s unique eloquence, and the ways his life and work combined into his singular vision.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Adriano Aprà

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: The Mystery Inc. gang from Hanna-Barbera’s classic cartoon, Scooby-Doo, Where Are You! took their sleuthing skills to the big screen with their first live-action adventure in 2002’s Scooby-Doo . Led by ‘90s teen heartthrobs and real-life couple Freddie Prinze Jr. and Sarah Michelle Gellar as Fred and Daphne, the amateur detectives Velma (Linda Cardellini), Shaggy (Matthew Lillard) and his best friend, the cowardly, always hungry, and vocal Great Dane, Scooby-Doo, reunite to solve the mystery of ghostly happenings at the tropical resort Spooky Island. From a script co-written by James Gunn and featuring Rowan Atkinson as the eccentric resort-owner, the film was a box office success on its release and continues to have an avid following.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Raja Gosnell

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Snow White, orphaned as a child, is forced to work under the reign of her evil stepmother, the Queen, who will stop at nothing to remain the most beautiful being in the land. When Snow White’s beauty grows, so does the Queen’s jealously. Seething with hatred, the Queen concocts a sinister plan to put an end to her. Will the princess escape her fate and achieve her happily ever after? Based on the classic Brothers Grimm fairy tale, this first animated feature from The Walt Disney Company—and the first traditionally animated feature ever produced— was nominated for its original score; the following year, the Academy gave Disney a Special Award for the film (one full-sized Oscar and seven small ones), “recognized as a significant screen innovation which has charmed millions and pioneered a great new entertainment field for the motion picture cartoon.”
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: David Hand, Perce Pearce, William Cottrell, Larry Morey, Wilfred Jackson, Ben Sharpsteen PRODUCED BY: Walt Disney

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Billy Wilder

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: In a small, boring town, best friends Jim and Will eagerly await the excitement of the yearly carnival. But after a different festival, helmed by the sinister Mr. Dark, unexpectedly sets up overnight, the town adults begin to fall under his spell, and the funfair reveals itself as a carnival of terror. Disney funded the project, based on Ray Bradbury’s short story “Black Ferris,” in hopes of breaking free from its stereotype of animated family films; ultimately, there were extensive edits and reshoots to create a more family-friendly film without losing too many of the thrills.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Jack Clayton PRODUCED BY: Peter Vincent Douglas

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Three men search a dangerous, restricted area known as the Zone looking for a secret room that supposedly grants wishes. Director Andrei Tarkovsky ( Solaris , 1972) faced unusual hardships during production, including a literally toxic location and problems with film stock that forced nearly an entire film’s worth of reshoots. But the result—one of Tarkovsky's boldest and most challenging projects—has been cited as an influential work by directors and production designers, with its stark and evocative imagery credited to Tarkovsky himself as art director, working with Aleksandr Boym and set decorator Rashit Safiullin.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Andrei Tarkovsky

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Named for the volcanic island in the Tyrrhenian Sea, Rossellini's first collaboration with Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman is a heartbreaking tale about a young Baltic woman who follows an Italian fisherman to his tiny, isolated village. Married swiftly after their release from an internment camp, she begins to struggle as her refined upbringing clashes with the rough local lifestyle, causing strain on her marriage and her psyche. It was Bergman who first contacted Rossellini after seeing Paisàn in 1948 in hopes of collaborating, and the making of Stromboli marks the beginning of a love affair that ended the filmmaker’s marriage and caused an international scandal when Bergman announced their pregnancy. For Rossellini, the project also signals a creative shift, at least to some critics, away from realism and into a deeply psychological phase.

In Paul Verhoeven’s stylish, psychological-erotic thriller, author Gerard (Jeroen Krabbé), begins a romantic affair with Christine (Renée Soutendijk), an enigmatic widow from literary society, only to become obsessed with her lover, Herman (Thom Hoffman). While continuing the affair in hopes of getting closer to Herman, Gerard is plagued by ominous visions, fueling paranoid thoughts about Christine plotting murder. Based on the novel by celebrated Dutch author Gerard Reve, The 4th Man was Verhoeven’s final film shot in Dutch before directing English-language and Hollywood productions. It was the Netherlands’ official submission for International Feature Film at the 56th Academy Awards, and, upon its release in the US, gave American audiences a taste of Verhoeven’s unabashed take on sex, violence, and religion.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Paul Verhoeven

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Two drag queens and a transgender woman drive across the Australian outback in a tour bus named Priscilla, in this wild road comedy that earned Lizzy Gardiner and Tim Chappell Oscars for their imaginative costume designs. Terence Stamp gives an impressive change-of-pace performance as the world-weary Bernadette, and he’s matched by Hugo Weaving as the trio’s conflicted leader. Guy Pearce delivers a breakout performance as the youngest of the group. Deftly mixing campy humor and genuine emotion amidst stunning locations, Priscilla was an international success and spawned a hit stage musical.

A student from a Virginian girl's school during the American Civil War discovers a Union Army corporal wounded in the woods and takes him in. Attracted to the handsome enemy soldier, the women of the home allow him to stay. This intense gothic thriller is filled with jealousy, rage, and betrayals. Based on the 1966 novel by Thomas P. Cullinan, this adaptation stars Colin Farrell, Nicole Kidman, Elle Fanning, and Kirsten Dunst. The Beguiled earned director Sofia Coppola the Prix de la mise en scene (Best Director Award) at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Sofia Coppola PRODUCED BY: Youree Henley, Sofia Coppola

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: A spin-off of Whisper of the Heart, The Cat Returns finds another schoolgirl encountering a mysterious tomcat on the street, though this time she is led to a fantastic world beyond her wildest dreams. Launched into a cobblestoned magic kingdom ruled by cat royalty—including a motorcade replete with vassals, maidens, and even Secret Service—she must enlist the help of the elusive Baron Humbert von Gikkingen (the same cat featured as a statue in Whisper of the Heart) if she hopes to make it back home. The only feature film directed by Hiroyuki Morita to date, The Cat Returns is a feline flight of fancy.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Hiroyuki Morita

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: The second film from Dena Enterprises, the production company founded by actor Danny Kaye ( White Christmas, 1954) and his songwriter wife, Sylvia Fine, The Court Jester is a delightful vehicle for the comedic icon to showcase his unparalleled timing, physical humor, and witty wordplay. Kaye is Hubert Hawkins, a retired carnival performer who disguises himself as a jester to help overturn an evil plot against a rightful British king. This ridiculous romp, with undeniable star Kaye at its center, is buttressed by a sincere Glynis Johns ( Mary Poppins , 1964) as Maid Jean and an arch Basil Rathbone ( Sherlock Holmes, 1939–1946) as Lord Ravenhurst. The most expensive comedy ever made at the time, primarily for its lavish sets, The Court Jester earned Kaye a Golden Globe nomination, and in 2004, the National Film Registry added the film to its list of titles considered “culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant.”

Olivia Colman won the Best Actress Oscar for her richly detailed performance as England’s Queen Anne, who finds two women competing for her affections in their quest for power: the aristocratic Lady Sarah (supporting actress nominee Rachel Weisz) and the impoverished Abigail Hill (supporting actress nominee Emma Stone). Working from a darkly comic, fact-based screenplay by Deborah Davis and Tony McNamara, director Yorgos Lanthimos ( Poor Things , 2023) subverts the cliches of historical dramas to startling effect. The Favourite’s 10 nominations include Best Picture, Directing and Original Screenplay. Nominated production designer Fiona Crombie and set decorator Alice Felton used a stark, black-and-white palate for their regal settings, matching Sandy Powell’s elegant, nominated costume designs.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Yorgos Lanthimos

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Inspired by the writings of Saint Francis of Assisi and the hagiographic texts about his loyal follower Brother Juniper, The Flowers of St. Francis is composed of simple vignettes that beautifully illustrate the humane life lessons of the People’s Saint. Using only one professional actor, with the rest of the cast comprised of friars from the Franciscan monastery, Rossellini’s film brings into focus, as he put it in 1950, “the merrier aspect of the Franciscan experience, the playfulness, the ‘perfect delight,’ the freedom that the spirit finds in poverty, and in absolute detachment from material things.”

In the small coastal California town of Antonio Bay, an old local is spinning tales of a ghostly fog to children on the beach, evoking terrors from 100 years earlier. As the clock strikes midnight, the fog and its vengeful spirits return, once again wreaking havoc. The Fog is seen as a welcome return to the horror genre for Carpenter after the monumental success of Halloween (1978). John Carpenter directs Jamie Lee Curtis, Adrienne Barbeau, and John Houseman through the haunting of Antonio Bay.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Debra Hill

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: “Doc” McCoy (Steve McQueen) is unexpectedly freed from a lengthy prison sentence to take part in a bank robbery, but there may be no one he can trust, not even his seemingly loyal wife (Ali MacGraw). For one of his first produced screenplays, Walter Hill adapted one of noir master Jim Thompson’s darkest novels into a more light-hearted but still cynical romantic thriller, with director Sam Peckinpah staging the film’s action sequences with his usual vividness.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Sam Peckinpah PRODUCED BY: David Foster, Mitchell Brower

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Fast-talking Rosalind Russell ( His Girl Friday , 1940) is absolutely captivating as Kim Halliday, the daughter of a deceased career gambler who joins her father’s former business partner to run a Vegas casino. Russell's unflappable confidence is a fine match for the swagger of Fernando Lamas as Victor Monte, a rival club owner who vies for Kim’s affections—and her casino. There’s nothing quite like the neon lights of Sin City captured in high-definition VistaVision and vibrant Technicolor, which appear here in gorgeous documentary footage of the Strip; like most studio productions of the era, however, the bulk of this musical comedy was shot on producer Paramount’s lot.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Robert Pirosh

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Writer-director Wes Anderson was inspired by Austrian novelist Stefan Zweig (1881-1942) for his seriocomic and visually dazzling story about a posh resort, its vain concierge (Ralph Fiennes in a peerless comic performance) and a young lobby boy (Tony Revolori). Anderson directed an all-star international cast and brought his distinctive visual sensibilities to his original story (written with Hugo Guinness), set in a fictional European country on the eve of war. The film received nine nominations including Best Picture and won Oscars for Alexandre Desplat’s effervescent score, Milena Canonero’s costume design, the makeup and hair creations of Frances Hannon and Mark Coulier, and the production design of Adam Stockhausen and his set decorator, Anna Pinnock, who transformed a vacant German department store into the eponymous hotel.

Based on the iconic Disneyland ride, The Haunted Mansion stars Eddie Murphy as real estate agent Jim Evers, a workaholic who wants to close a mansion deal before going on a much-needed vacation with his wife, Sara, and his kids. Upon their arrival, the family is lured apart by ghosts who believe Sara can set them free by joining them in the afterlife. The Evers family battles ghosts, zombies, and spiders to save Sara from eternal damnation, also encountering – of course -- references to the amusement park ride, including Hidden Mickeys and the theme song, “Grim Grinning Ghosts.”
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Rob Minkoff PRODUCED BY: Don Hahn, Andrew Gunn

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: This gritty biopic dives into the smoky, dangerous glamor of Prohibition-era Chicago for the true story of nightclub performer Joe E. Lewis, famous for being one of the few people who could make gangster Al Capone laugh. Crooner Frank Sinatra, lauded by the film's marketing as “the most electric personality of our time,” follows Lewis’s highs and lows with the same realism and range he brought to The Man with the Golden Arm (1955). Ol’ Blue Eyes also adds musical dimension to the character — the real Lewis was more comedian than singer—with director Charles Vidor (no relation to fellow director King) compounding his experience with musicals and comedies into a story with dramatic nuance.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Charles Vidor

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: In the early 20th century, the last princess of the Korean royal family under Japanese rule is forced to move to Japan to attend school, leaving behind her family, friends, and the only home she has ever known. Kim Jang-han (Park Hae-il), a childhood friend and Japanese army officer, helps to plan an escape route for her. This film, based on the real story of Princess Deokhye (Son Ye-jin), weaves fact with fiction to retell the story of a once-lost princess who stopped at nothing to return to the home she yearned for. –note written by Hannah Farkas.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Hur Jin-ho

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Friendless, plagued by nightmares, Tony Thompson, 8, struggles to adapt to his new home in Scotland and reconcile his obsession with vampires. His nightmares seem to come true when he meets child vampire Rudolph, though the two boys quickly become friends when they realize Tony’s nightmares contain essential information for Rudolph to break a centuries-old curse. Based on Angela Sommer-Bodenburg's children’s book series of the same name, this charming and whimsical tale of finding friendship in unlikely places is populated with eerie cemeteries, beautifully designed aristocratic costumes, and, of course, vampire cows.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Uli Edel PRODUCED BY: Richard Claus

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: One of Roberto Rossellini's most singular and unheralded works, this potent blend of neorealism and fantasy is an idiosyncratic, lighthearted fable. In a fishing village on the Amalfi Coast, a stranger claiming to be a saint bestows a photographer’s camera with the power to kill bad people by photographing existing pictures of them. Initially, the photographer uses his newfound weapon to eliminate abusers of power. But before long, he succumbs to the very same amoral selfishness he once claimed to despise. When asked in a 1970 interview whether the film was about filmmaking, Rossellini replied, "It's rather a game, an attempt at comedy, [...] an isolated experiment."
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Salvo D’Angelo

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Penned by Arthur Miller, this contemporary Western centers on the recently divorced Roslyn (Marilyn Monroe) and her relationship with an aging former cowboy, Gay (Clark Gable), who now survives by rounding up wild mustangs to sell them to a slaughterhouse. Considered a commercial failure at the time of its original release, the film has since been regarded as a classic by critics and audiences, perhaps notably because it was the final completed film of both Gable and Monroe, and a fitting bookend to Monroe’s career—she credited Huston for her first big break in his The Asphalt Jungle (1950).
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: John Huston PRODUCED BY: Frank E. Taylor

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Sean Crenshaw (Andre Gower) is the leader of his school's monster club, a group of monster- and horror film-loving pre-teens who get the thrill of their lives when their favorite on-screen creatures show up in their own backyard. As Dracula, Wolf-Man, Gill-Man, and the Mummy join forces to steal a magical amulet and take over the world, it is up to these plucky kids to use their knowledge of horror tropes to stop them. The movie struggled to find an audience, thanks in part to its newly created PG-13 rating, but it has achieved cult status among horror fans, with many citing it as the film that sparked their love for genre as children. Please note: This film contains the use of homophobic language.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Fred Dekker PRODUCED BY: Jonathan A. Zimbert

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Grace Stewart (Nicole Kidman) keeps the curtains drawn at all hours of the day in her opulent manor to protect her children, Anne and Nicholas, from crippling photosensitivity. When three travelers appear in search of work, Grace hires them to tend to the home and the children, noting the previous employees “vanished” just days ago. The arrival of the new workers seems to trigger paranormal incidents throughout the home. Set in 1945 Jersey, United Kingdom, this brooding psychological horror highlights the depths of Kidman’s range and Amenábar’s imagination.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Alejandro Amenábar

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Two illusionists compete at the turn of the 20th century to create history’s greatest magic trick in this time-fracturing thriller from director/co-writer Christopher Nolan. Based on the 1995 novel by Christopher Priest, the film earned Oscar nominations for its cinematography (Wally Pfister) and art direction (Nathan Crowley, Julie Ochipinti), which cleverly used surviving Los Angeles picture palaces as key locations. The stellar cast includes Hugh Jackman and Christian Bale as the rivals, Michael Caine as their mentor, Scarlett Johansson and Rebecca Hall as the women in their lives, and a memorable cameo from David Bowie as the inventor Nikola Tesla.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Christopher Nolan

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: When the family of Civil War veteran Ethan Edwards (John Wayne) is killed in a Comanche raid, he spends years looking for his kidnapped niece—but her uncle may prove more of a threat than her abductors. John Ford’s epic, morally complex Western drama has become one of his most revered films in the 70 years since its release. It has been cited as a favorite by many filmmakers, including Francis Ford Coppola, Martin Scorsese and Steven Spielberg, and has influenced films as diverse as Star Wars (1977) and Hardcore (1979). Three-time Oscar winner Winton C. Hoch ( The Quiet Man, 1952) shot the film in VistaVision on stunning outdoor locations, including Monument Valley, culminating in a powerful, frequently imitated final image.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: John Ford

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Debut director Hiromasa Yonebayashi ( When Marnie Was There, 2014) and Studio Ghibli teamed up for this film version of Mary Norton’s 1952 children’s classic The Borrowers , full of gorgeous imagery of the natural world. Arrietty is the daughter of a family of Borrowers—miniature people secretly living in an occupied house—who risk their home when she befriends a human boy.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Hiromasa Yonebayashi

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: One of Monroe’s most successful roles was as The Girl in director Billy Wilder’s The Seven Year Itch , a comedy about a restless husband left to his own devices for the summer. To market the film, photographer Sam Shaw proposed the indelible subway grate moment, which dozens of publicity photographers attended on location in New York City. Due to sound issues, the real scene was shot on the 20th Century-Fox lot in Los Angeles. Outside of this iconic scene, the exhibition Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon also features silk pajamas worn during a pivotal moment in developing Monroe’s girl-next-door character.

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: The final film directed by blockbuster master Cecil B. DeMille is a lavish remake of his own 1923 silent epic. Charlton Heston, as Moses, leads a stellar cast, including Yul Brynner as Pharaoh Rameses II, Anne Baxter as the lustful Nefretiri, and Edward G. Robinson as the rebellious Dathan. The film was nominated for seven Oscars, including Best Picture, and John Fulton ( The Invisible Man , 1933) won for its special effects, which included such classic Biblical sequences as the Burning bush, the Ten Plagues, and the parting of the Red Sea.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Cecil B. DeMille

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Terrence Malick adapted James Jones’s 1962 novel, inspired by the author’s experiences serving in World War II’s Guadalcanal campaign, for his first film since his 1978 classic Days of Heaven . Malick assembled an all-star cast (including George Clooney, Nick Nolte and John Travolta) for his unusually contemplative war epic, which received seven Oscar nominations including Directing, Adapted Screenplay (both for Malick) and Best Picture. Nominated composer Hans Zimmer spent nine months working on his evocative score, which he termed the most challenging assignment of his career.

In the first installment of what Carpenter would later call his Apocalypse Trilogy, a research team in Antarctica runs afoul of a shapeshifting alien menace. This bleak and stylish sci-fi horror thriller features Kurt Russell as resourceful helicopter pilot MacReady and Bill Lancaster’s screenplay in a faithful adaptation of John W. Campbell’s 1938 novella Who Goes There? , which was first filmed in 1951 as The Thing from Another World . Upon release, Carpenter’s film was overlooked in favor of Steven Spielberg’s record-breaking, friendly alien adventure E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), but in the ensuing decades, The Thing has become a contemporary classic, influencing many filmmakers. It was selected for preservation in the National Film Registry by the Library of Congress in 2025.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: David Foster, Lawrence Turman

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Starring in Yeon Sang-ho’s intimate suspense drama is Park Jeong-min, in his compelling portrayal of Dong-hwan and the younger version of his father, Yeong-gyu, in flashback sequences. Yeong-gyu, who cannot see, is a renowned wooden seal carver, respected for his intricate craftsmanship. Dong-hwan has no memory of his mother, who has been missing for 40 years—or so he’s been told—until he receives a startling call about her remains. Adapted from his own graphic novel, Yeon excavates the ugly aspects of societal standards and perceptions of beauty, and unapologetically exhibits the dark sides of human greed, desire, and trauma.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Yeon Sang-ho

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Internationally renowned fine artist Tacita Dean presents her rarely screened The Uncles (2004), in which the sons of Ealing Studios icons Basil Dean and Sir Michael Balcon reflect on their fathers’ careers and personal lives in an extended conversation with historian and curator Laurence Kardish. Filmed and projected in anamorphic 16mm, The Uncles offers an unusual widescreen portrait of two loquacious, charming English gentlemen (Winton Dean and Jonathan Balcon) illuminating the accomplishments, failings, and elusive humanity of their eminent fathers with wit, candor, and understated complexity. Beyond the copious anecdotal nuggets of interest to any fan of classic British cinema, the film also grants intimate access to two men who both admired and struggled to truly know their fathers as they consider their own youths in pre-war Britain. In conjunction with this screening and organized by Los Angeles’ Marciano Art Foundation (MAF) director Hanneke Skerath and Mark Toscano, MAF will present the US debut of Dean’s landmark installation, FILM (2011), from September 18, 2026, through January 2, 2027. Program and notes by Academy Film Archive Senior Film Preservationist Mark Toscano.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Tacita Dean

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accessible screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume for viewers who are neurodiverse. They walk among us, often appearing as ordinary women, but when one notices those purple eyes, gloved hands, and keen smell for children, it can mean only one thing: a witch. Luke, an orphaned 9-year-old, is vacationing in a seaside hotel with his grandma. So is an undercover witch convention. After the Grand High Witch turns Luke into a mouse, he finds himself scurrying to save the rest of the world’s children from a similar fate. This wicked tale, adapted from Roald Dahl’s children’s novel of the same name, features the work of Jim Henson’s Creature Shop in the iconic and terrifying reveal of the witches' true forms, and an unforgettable performance by Anjelica Huston as the Grand High Witch.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Nicolas Roeg PRODUCED BY: Mark Shivas

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Co-written by Anita Loos and Jane Murfin, The Women delivers 135 of them, each with a speaking role, to the exclusion of men. The delightfully witty and rapid-fire dialogue pours out of a cadre of familiar faces, including Norma Shearer, Joan Crawford, and Rosalind Russell. While most of the film unfolds in black-and-white, a delightful six-minute Technicolor fashion show is included, featuring gowns by Adrian, the iconic, MGM-based costume designer. Contributing to the distinctive looks of the cast was the uncredited hair designer, MGM veteran Sydney Guilaroff, whose film career spanned the 1930s to the 1980s and included such classics as Singin’ in the Rain (1952), North by Northwest (1959) and Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966)
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: George Cukor PRODUCED BY: Hunt Stromberg

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: The Donahue clan, led by husband and wife Molly and Terry (Ethel Merman and Dan Dailey), navigate the ups and downs of show biz, from their beginnings in Vaudeville to the Great Depression, in this musical comedy with songs by Irving Berlin. The family’s close bond is further tested with the arrival of the talented and driven Vicky Parker (Marilyn Monroe). Costume designer Travilla played an integral role in shaping Marilyn Monroe’s public image on- and off-screen. Together they famously produced looks that evaded censorship while still courting controversy. His designs for her showgirl characters are of particular note.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Walter Lang PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

Costume designer Travilla played an integral role in shaping Marilyn Monroe’s public image on- and off-screen. Together they famously produced looks that evaded censorship while still courting controversy. His designs for her showgirl characters are of particular note.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Walter Lang PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Before Terrence Malick’s Badlands (1973), before Arthur Penn’s Bonnie and Clyde (1967), there was Nicholas Ray’s They Live by Night (1948), a book-to-screen adaptation about young lovers on the run. After busting out of prison, Bowie (Farley Granger) hides out at a filling station owned by a dad with alcoholism and his daughter Keechie (Cathy O’Donnell) and starts knocking off banks with his fellow escapees. After a spending spree leaves Bowie injured and vulnerable to the law, Keechie falls for him, and the couple sets off an ill-fated journey, hopeful for a new life. In Ray’s remarkable debut feature, classic noir elements blend effortlessly with melodrama to create something entirely new, making They Live by Night a standout of the period, realized with lived-in dialogue beautifully adapted from Edward Anderson’s source material and shot primarily on location in greater Los Angeles. The film is notable too for its innovative camera techniques and tracking shots, especially in the driving sequences. This warm-up for Rebel Without a Cause (1955) finds Ray arriving on the scene fully formed with a confident and inimitable style. A favorite of cartoonist Nathan Gelgud and critic A. S. Hamrah, the screening is followed by a conversation about Ray and his oft-overlooked influence on American filmmaking. In a separately ticketed event before the film, Gelgud and Hamrah sign copies of their newest books. Programmed and note by K.J. Relth-Miller.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Nicholas Ray PRODUCED BY: John Houseman

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: When a drifter looking for work stumbles upon a pair of sunglasses that reveal the ruling class as a colonizing alien race, he sets out to expose and destroy the invaders. Roddy Piper and Keith David star as down-on-their-luck, working class men who discover that these undercover aliens are broadcasting subliminal messages, encouraging conformity and consumerism in a plot to rule Earth. Unabashed in its social and political commentary, They Live reflects John Carpenter’s distaste for Reagan-era politics and commercialism. Based on Ray Nelson’s short story “Eight O’Clock in the Morning” and scored by Carpenter, the film has developed a strong cult following and continues to find new fans with messaging that still resonates in our current political climate.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Larry Franco

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: A Shakespearean actor reluctantly joins a Resistance plot against the Nazis in 1939 Warsaw in this daring comedy directed by two-time Oscar nominee Ernst Lubitsch ( Heaven Can Wait, 1943). Comedy legend Jack Benny had his greatest screen role as the pompous ham Joseph Tura, and Oscar nominee Carole Lombard ( My Man Godfrey , 1936) was his expert match as his actress wife, Maria, her final film role before her death weeks before the film’s release. Finding the perfect balance between wartime tension and hilarious farce, Lubitsch’s classic— filmed right as the U.S. entered World War II— was remade in 1983, with Mel Brooks and Anne Bancroft as the couple.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Ernst Lubitsch

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: John Robie (Cary Grant), a former French Resistance fighter and cat burglar, is enjoying his early retirement in the Riviera when a series of thefts make him once more the prime suspect—and for the beautiful heiress Frances Stevens (Grace Kelly), these suspicions only add to his appeal. Alfred Hitchcock paired two of Hollywood’s most effortlessly glamorous stars for this witty combination of romantic comedy and caper thriller, adapted by John Michael Hayes ( Rear Window , 1954) from the novel by David Dodge. The Oscar-winning VistaVision cinematography of Hitchcock’s regular collaborator Robert Burks ( Strangers on a Train , 1951) captures the beauty of the co-stars and the setting in all its splendor.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Alfred Hitchcock

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: An American tap dancer pursues the woman he loves from London to Venice in the fourth movie musical to feature the iconic team of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, and the second of their films to receive a Best Picture nomination, following The Gay Divorcee (1934). Spotlighting the stars at their effortless best, it was also nominated for Irving Berlin’s classic “Cheek to Cheek,” Hermes Pan’s dance direction of the numbers “Piccolino” and “Top Hat, White Tie, and Tails,” and the art direction of Van Nest Polglase and Carroll Clark, whose elegant deco sets include a Venice canal constructed on a Los Angeles soundstage.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Mark Sandrich

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: With the South Korean peninsula in the throes of a national disaster, travelers board the KTX, a fast a train to Busan, a city unaffected by the crisis. Among them is Seok-woo, a workaholic father traveling with his daughter. When a young woman, scuffed and dazed, gets on board, an unimaginable horror erupts in the train’s claustrophobic confines. Director Yeon Sang-ho, whose prior filmmaking comprises groundbreaking animated features, balances an upbeat, kinetic energy with solid emotional storytelling to deliver much more than just an action-driven genre film.

Diane Lane received an Oscar nomination for her remarkable portrayal of Connie Sumner, who lives an admirable life in an upper-class neighborhood of upstate New York with loving husband Edward and 8-year-old son Charlie. In a gush of wind, an unpredictable encounter occurs between Connie and an attractive man in the street of New York City, followed by the irreversible measures of an illicit affair. Adrian Lyne candidly and without judgment surveys on lust, passion, jealousy, and guilt, unearthing a dark, dense pool of human emotion and the arbitrariness of its motivation.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Adrian Lyne

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Vampires in 4K Based on John Steakley’s novel of the same name, John Carpenter’s Vampires is the master of horror’s sole foray into the realm of vampirism. The film may be full of style and tropes influenced by classic Westerns, including a setting in New Mexico, but the heroes brandish wooden stakes and crossbows instead of rifles and six-shooters. Jack Crow (James Woods) leads a team of grizzled, Vatican-sponsored vampire hunters who seek to exterminate Valek (Thomas Ian Griffith), the first vampire, now on a quest to gain immunity from the sun. Balancing action and one-liners with scares and gore, all set to a Carpenter score, Vampires is a fresh, contemporary take on the classic monsters of Universal and Hammer horror fame.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Sandy King

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Viva Ingrid! A moving documentary tribute to a mother, wife, and actress, this mix of home movies, newsreels, and clips from films by Roberto Rossellini paints a shortform portrait of three-time Academy Award-winning Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman, as realized by one of Rossellini’s grandsons.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Alessandro Rossellini

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Park Hae-il’s big-screen debut is Yim Soon-rye’s second feature, which received critical praise upon its 2001 release, establishing Yim as one of Korea’s most significant directors. Seong-woo, lead singer and guitarist of Waikiki Brothers—a band formed with his friends back in high school—returns to his hometown with his bandmates in hopes of repairing their fragile relationship. But the band stagnates, and Seong-woo is torn between a dream that’s out of reach and his thin grasp on reality. Park, who portrays the teen version of Seong-woo, generates youthful energy, evoking the purity that Seong-woo and his bandmates once carried and now long for. Yim’s insightful and humane perception of the cruel split between dreams and reality in modern Korea permeates this portrayal of her sympathetic and intricate characters.

The third film in the contemporary version of the Planet of the Apes series finds the ape leader Caesar (another remarkable motion capture performance by Andy Serkis) seeking a safe haven for the survivors of a human-led massacre, only to wind up in a labor camp run by a vicious military officer (Woody Harrelson). The film was nominated for the visual effects by Joe Letteri, Daniel Barrett, Dan Lemmon and Joel Whist, who depict the film’s ape characters and wintry, post-apocalyptic setting with astonishing realism.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Matt Reeves PRODUCED BY: Peter Chernin, Dylan Clark, Rick Jaffa, Amanda Silver

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: The director of Coraline (2009) and The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993) brings his eerie whimsy to a macabre tale of an orphaned punk, Kat. Haunted by her parents' death and disappointed with other adults, she is shuttled off to a failing boarding school, where she discovers her ability to summon demons. Two of them, voiced by Keegan-Michael Key and Jordan Peele, manipulate Kat into bringing them to the land of the living with a promise of resurrecting her parents, but bringing people back from the dead never turns out quite as planned. With spectacular stop-motion animation, an inspired Afro-punk soundtrack, and kooky antics aplenty, this is a charming take on the importance of community, standing up for what's right, and befriending your demons.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Henry Selick PRODUCED BY: Henry Selick, Ellen Goldsmith-Vein, Jordan Peele, Win Rosenfeld

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: “It isn’t fair! Here we are, three desperate criminals who will stop at nothing to escape from Devil’s Island, and we have to fall in with nice people!” So laments Jules (Peter Ustinov), one of a trio of convicts stuck on the French-controlled isle on Christmas Eve, 1895, where they fall in with the lovely proprietors of a local supply shop. Crime, romance, and dark comedy collide in an entertaining tale of unexpected guardian angels from director and star of Casablanca (1942) Michael Curtiz and Humphrey Bogart, with the actor in a rare comedic role. The material was rich enough for director Neil Jordan to revisit in 1989, this time with Oscar-winning stars Robert De Niro and Sean Penn.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Michael Curtiz

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: This popular musical comedy inspired by Irving Berlin’s Oscar-winning song from Holiday Inn (1942) was the first feature to be filmed and released in VistaVision. Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye star as war veterans and entertainers who become romantically involved with a sister act (Rosemary Clooney and Vera-Ellen). Directed by Oscar winner Michael Curtiz ( Casablanca , 1943), White Christmas features delightful musical numbers spotlighting more than a dozen Irving Berlin songs, including the nominated “Count Your Blessings (Instead of Sheep)”.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Michael Curtiz

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Eddie Valiant (Bob Hoskins), a private eye in 1930s Los Angeles, gets an unexpected client—Roger Rabbit, a cartoon film star. Director Robert Zemeckis’s witty comedy-mystery is a dazzling mix of live-action and animation, incorporating beloved cartoon characters from Disney and other studios. Nominated for its art direction, cinematography, and sound, it won for its film editing, sound effects editing, and visual effects. Richard Williams also received a Special Achievement Award from the Academy for his animation direction.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Robert Zemeckis

https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accommodative screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume specifically for neurodivergent viewers. When a young rabbit from Bunnyburrow moves to the big city of Zootopia to achieve her lifelong dream of becoming a police officer, she uncovers a sinister conspiracy. She also develops an unexpected friendship with a wily fox in this computer-animated comedy that imaginatively depicts a metropolis populated by animals of every type. The winner of the 2016 Animated Feature Film Oscar, Zootopia benefits from its expert voice cast, led by Ginnifer Goodwin as the bunny cop, Jason Bateman as the cynical fox, and Idris Elba as the world-weary Cape buffalo police chief.
https://www.academymuseum.org/en/program.director: Byron Howard, Rich Moore
